title: Why Fewer American Children Are Living in Poverty

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 回想我在黑胶唱片时代在夜店当DJ的时候，每天晚上你都要带300件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，你把DJ台

sentences.en: into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成了一个活生生的、充满美丽50年历史文物的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times,
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔维内西，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: The high poverty rate among American children was long seen as an enduring fact of American life.
sentences.zh: 美国儿童的高贫困率长期以来被视为美国生活中一个挥之不去的事实。

sentences.en: But a new analysis shows that in recent decades, it has declined dramatically.
sentences.zh: 但一项新的分析显示，在过去的几十年里，这一数字急剧下降。

sentences.en: Today, I speak with my colleague Jason DeParle about the remarkable drop in child poverty and the surprising reasons behind it.
sentences.zh: 今天，我与我的同事杰森·德帕勒一起探讨儿童贫困率的显著下降及其背后的惊人原因。

sentences.en: It's Monday, September 26th.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月26日，星期一。

sentences.en: Jason, you wrote a series of stories recently about this really remarkable decline in the number of American children who live in poverty.
sentences.zh: 杰森，你最近写了一系列关于生活在贫困中的美国儿童数量显着下降的报道。

sentences.en: Tell us about your reporting.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲你的报道吧。

sentences.en: Sabrina, I started covering poverty issues in the 1980s when more than a quarter of American children were poor.
sentences.zh: 萨布丽娜，我从20世纪80年代开始报道贫困问题，当时超过四分之一的美国儿童生活在贫困之中。

sentences.en: And the number just didn't move from year to year.
sentences.zh: 而且这个数字年复一年地毫无变化。

sentences.en: It was stuck.
sentences.zh: 它停滞不前了。

sentences.en: It seemed like a problem that American society just didn't know how to fix.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是一个美国社会根本不知道如何解决的问题。

sentences.en: You know, Ronald Reagan famously said the federal government declared war on poverty and poverty won.
sentences.zh: 你知道，罗纳德·里根曾有一句名言：联邦政府宣战了贫困，结果贫困赢了。

sentences.en: So there was a sense of fatalism about the ability to erase this moral stain out of American society.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们对于消除美国社会这一道德污点的能力有一种宿命论的心态。

sentences.en: And then one day I was looking at a graph and I saw something starting to change.
sentences.zh: 然后有一天，我看着一张图表，看到了一些开始发生变化的东西。

sentences.en: The share of American children in poverty was declining substantially.
sentences.zh: 生活在贫困中的美国儿童比例在大幅下降。

sentences.en: And I decided to look further to understand what was happening with low-income children in America and what were the forces behind it.
sentences.zh: 我决定进一步深入了解美国低收入儿童的情况以及背后的推动力。

sentences.en: And I found that over the course of a generation, child poverty fell 59%.
sentences.zh: 我发现，在一代人的时间里，儿童贫困率下降了59%。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: The share of children in poverty went from more than one in four back in 1993 to about one in 10 today.
sentences.zh: 生活在贫困中的儿童比例从1993年的超过四分之一下降到如今的约十分之一。

sentences.en: It was a huge drop.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的降幅。

sentences.en: A huge drop, yes.
sentences.zh: 确实是个巨大的降幅。

sentences.en: And why was that the case?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样呢？

sentences.en: I mean, what had happened?
sentences.zh: 我是说，究竟发生了什么？

sentences.en: One thing that happened was that the Census Bureau changed the way it was measuring poverty.
sentences.zh: 发生的一件事是，人口普查局改变了其衡量贫困的方式。

sentences.en: Traditionally, the government measured child poverty while leaving out the impact of most safety net prograMs.
sentences.zh: 传统上，政府在衡量儿童贫困时排除了大多数安全网项目的影响。

sentences.en: So the government delivers tens of billions of dollars a year in wage subsidies through tax credits, in nutritional aid, through food stamps, in housing assistance,
sentences.zh: 因此，政府每年通过税收抵免提供数百亿美元的工资补贴，通过食品券提供营养援助，通过住房援助，

sentences.en: through programs like Section 8 and public housing.
sentences.zh: 通过第8条和公共住房等项目提供支持。

sentences.en: The old way of measuring poverty ignores all that aid.
sentences.zh: 旧的贫困衡量标准忽略了所有这些援助。

sentences.en: So the government could spend and spend and spend and seem to make no difference because it simply wasn't measuring the impact of that aid.
sentences.zh: 所以政府可以不断地投入资金，却似乎毫无作用，因为他们根本没有衡量这些援助的影响。

sentences.en: But in 2009, the government began using a new poverty measure, which does take into effect the impact of government aid.
sentences.zh: 但在2009年，政府开始使用一种新的贫困衡量标准，该标准确实考虑到了政府援助的影响。

sentences.en: And once you take that into account, you start to see that child poverty rates are going down significantly.
sentences.zh: 一旦你把这一点考虑进去，你就会开始发现儿童贫困率在显著下降。

sentences.en: So there's this new measure and it's kind of like x-ray glasses, right?
sentences.zh: 所以有了这个新标准，它有点像X光眼镜，对吧？

sentences.en: You couldn't see any of the effect at all.
sentences.zh: 你以前根本看不到任何效果。

sentences.en: And then suddenly you do because you put these glasses on and you realize, oh my gosh, there has been an effect.
sentences.zh: 然后突然间你看到了，因为你戴上了这副眼镜，你意识到，天哪，原来确实产生了效果。

sentences.en: That's exactly the reaction I had when I was looking at the graph, you know, it's like I put on different glasses.
sentences.zh: 这正是我看图表时的反应，你知道的，就像我戴上了不同的眼镜。

sentences.en: Wow, the line's going down.
sentences.zh: 哇，曲线在下降。

sentences.en: It's not going straight flat like it used to.
sentences.zh: 它不像以前那样笔直平坦了。

sentences.en: And things are getting better for low-income thermos.
sentences.zh: 低收入人群的情况正在变好。

sentences.en: That's good.
sentences.zh: 那很好。

sentences.en: There was a decline.
sentences.zh: 确实出现了下降。

sentences.en: But what actually caused that decline?
sentences.zh: 但究竟是什么导致了这种下降？

sentences.en: Well, Sabrina, lots of things shape child poverty.
sentences.zh: 嗯，萨布丽娜，有很多因素塑造了儿童贫困状况。

sentences.en: I mean, the economy grew.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，经济增长了。

sentences.en: We're a richer country than we were a generation ago.
sentences.zh: 我们比上一代人更富裕了。

sentences.en: Minimum wages grew when you take into account state-level increases in the minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 如果把州级最低工资的提高考虑在内，最低工资也增长了。

sentences.en: So people at the bottom saw their earnings rise somewhat.
sentences.zh: 因此，社会底层人们的收入有所增加。

sentences.en: Family living arrangements changed.
sentences.zh: 家庭居住安排发生了变化。

sentences.en: There are slightly more children living in two-parent households.
sentences.zh: 生活在双亲家庭的儿童稍微多了一些。

sentences.en: The share of children born to teen mothers has declined greatly.
sentences.zh: 未成年母亲所生孩子的比例大幅下降。

sentences.en: Lots of economic and demographic forces contributed to the decline in poverty.
sentences.zh: 许多经济和人口统计方面的力量共同促进了贫困率的下降。

sentences.en: But a dominant force was the expansion of government aid.
sentences.zh: 但其中一个主导力量是政府援助的扩张。

sentences.en: Okay, so tell me about that, this shift in the federal government's response to poverty.
sentences.zh: 好的，那么跟我讲讲这个，联邦政府对贫困应对方式的这种转变。

sentences.en: When do you see it really taking off?
sentences.zh: 你认为它是什么时候真正腾飞的？

sentences.en: Sabrina, I think the story begins in the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 萨布丽娜，我认为这个故事始于20世纪90年.

sentences.en: Welfare should be a second chance, not a way of life.
sentences.zh: 福利应该是一次机会，而不是一种生活方式。

sentences.en: When Bill Clinton ran for president as a reformist Democrat.
sentences.zh: 当时比尔·克林顿以改革派民主党人的身份竞选总统。

sentences.en: In my administration, we're going to put an end to welfare as we have come to know it.
sentences.zh: 在我的政府中，我们将结束我们所熟知的福利制度。

sentences.en: Pledging to end welfare as we know it.
sentences.zh: 发誓要结束我们所熟知的福利制度。

sentences.en: No more permanent dependence on welfare as a way of life.
sentences.zh: 不再对作为一种生活方式的福利产生永久性依赖。

sentences.en: By welfare, he meant one particular program called Aid to Families with Dependent Children.
sentences.zh: 他所说的福利是指一个特定的项目，叫做“援助有依赖孩子的家庭”。

sentences.en: It was the main cash welfare program for women with children.
sentences.zh: 这是针对有孩子的妇女的主要现金福利项目。

sentences.en: The program gave poor mothers a monthly cash payment.
sentences.zh: 该项目给贫困母亲每月发放现金补贴。

sentences.en: It wasn't a lot.
sentences.zh: 金额其实不多。

sentences.en: It was maybe $350 a month or so.
sentences.zh: 大概一个月350美元左右。

sentences.en: And critics of the program thought it was promoting two probleMs.
sentences.zh: 该项目的批评者认为它助长了两个问题。

sentences.en: Does welfare cause illegitimate birth?
sentences.zh: 福利会导致非婚生子女吗？

sentences.en: What the welfare system did was make it possible to take care of a baby without having a husband.
sentences.zh: 福利制度所做的是让人在没有丈夫的情况下也能养育孩子。

sentences.en: One, it was seen as encouraging women to have children outside of marriage, breaking up the family.
sentences.zh: 第一，它被视为鼓励女性在婚姻之外生育孩子，导致家庭破裂。

sentences.en: Why should we have to pay for you to sit at home, watch your soap operas?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们得花钱让你坐在家里看肥皂剧？

sentences.en: Some people are poor because of the value choices that they make in their behavior.
sentences.zh: 有些人贫困是因为他们在行为上做出了错误的价值选择。

sentences.en: And it was also seen as discouraging single mothers from going to work.
sentences.zh: 它还被视为阻碍单亲母亲出去工作。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So Clinton set out to effectively end this program.
sentences.zh: 所以克林顿着手有效地结束这个项目。

sentences.en: Well, I think most people thought what he would actually enact would be a modest reform.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想大多数人都认为他实际颁布的会是一项温和的改革。

sentences.en: But I would say to my friends in the Democratic Party that there is much to what Ronald Reagan was trying to get done.
sentences.zh: 但我要对民主党的朋友们说，罗纳德·里根试图完成的事情有很多可取之处。

sentences.en: And there's much we can share with each other.
sentences.zh: 我们之间有很多可以分享的共识。

sentences.en: Instead, Republicans heard this rhetoric, end welfare, and ran with it.
sentences.zh: 相反，共和党人听到了这种“结束福利”的言论，并借此大做文章。

sentences.en: We must replace the welfare state with an opportunity society.
sentences.zh: 我们必须用机会社会取代福利国家。

sentences.en: They took over Congress midway through his first term.
sentences.zh: 他在第一任期中途接管了国会。

sentences.en: We passed first in the House and now in the Senate a strong welfare reform bill.
sentences.zh: 我们先在众议院、后在参议院通过了一项强有力的福利改革法案。

sentences.en: I believe the president has an absolute moral obligation to sign this bill.
sentences.zh: 我相信总统有绝对的道德义务签署这项法案。

sentences.en: He campaigned in 1992, promising to end welfare as we know.
sentences.zh: 他在1992年竞选时承诺要结束我们所熟知的福利制度。

sentences.en: We're about to send him welfare reform.
sentences.zh: 我们正准备把福利改革法案送到他手上。

sentences.en: And to find ending welfare in a much more literal way than he had ever envisioned.
sentences.zh: 并以比他以往任何设想都更字面的方式去实现结束福利。

sentences.en: And so what was the outcome, Jason?
sentences.zh: 那么结果是什么呢，杰森？

sentences.en: The outcome was a law passed in 1996, which Clinton signed right before he ran for re-election that put strict time limits and work requirements on cash aid,
sentences.zh: 结果是1996年通过了一项法律，克林顿在竞选连任前夕签署了该法律，对现金援助规定了严格的时间限制和工作要求，

sentences.en: making it much harder for low-income mothers to get help when they were not working.
sentences.zh: 使得低收入母亲在不工作时更难获得帮助。

sentences.en: So half of Bill Clinton's legacy was the radical reduction of government assistance to one group of families, to single mothers who didn't work.
sentences.zh: 所以比尔·克林顿政治遗产的一半是对一组家庭——不工作的单亲母亲——大幅削减了政府援助。

sentences.en: But at the same time, you had a very large expansion of aid to low-income families who did work.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，你对那些工作的低收入家庭的援助进行了非常大幅度的扩张。

sentences.en: And that's because public officials, particularly Republicans, became more sympathetic to low-income people when they were working than when they weren't.
sentences.zh: 这是因为公众官员，尤其是共和党人，对有工作的低收入人群比对不工作的人更有同情心。

sentences.en: There was more sympathy, more political support for aiding the working poor.
sentences.zh: 对援助有工作的穷人有更多的同情和政治支持。

sentences.en: And I think that second trend got less attention.
sentences.zh: 我认为第二个趋势受到的关注较少。

sentences.en: The passage of the 1996 welfare bill helped shift the political dynamics of poverty and made it easier to pass expansions of aid to the working poor.
sentences.zh: 1996年福利法案的通过改变了贫困问题的政治动态，并使得更容易通过针对有工作穷人的援助扩张法案。

sentences.en: So effectively, there was this big shift in assistance from poor people who weren't working to poor people who were working.
sentences.zh: 因此，实际上，援助对象发生了一个重大转变，从不工作的穷人转向了工作的穷人。

sentences.en: That's true, but it wasn't just taking money from one group of people and giving it to a different group of people.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，但这不仅仅是从一群人那里拿走钱并分给另一群人。

sentences.en: Overall spending on low-income families grew.
sentences.zh: 对低收入家庭的总体支出增长了。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Okay, so tell us how the government expanded its spending for poor people.
sentences.zh: 好的，那么告诉我们政府是如何扩大对穷人的支出的。

sentences.en: I think a number of programs are relevant to this story.
sentences.zh: 我认为有许多项目与这个故事有关。

sentences.en: But to really understand the decline in child poverty, you have to understand something called the earned income tax credit.
sentences.zh: 但要真正理解儿童贫困率的下降，你必须了解一项名为“劳动所得税收抵免”的东西。

sentences.en: Oh, boy.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: It sounds really opaque, technocratic, something your accountant checks off on your form once a year.
sentences.zh: 听起来真的很晦涩、官僚，就像你会计一年在表格上勾选一次的东西。

sentences.en: But what it really is, is a system of annual bonuses, cash bonuses, checks in the mail to low-income families.
sentences.zh: 但它实际上是一套年度奖金系统，是发给低收入家庭的现金奖金、寄到家里的支票。

sentences.en: Pretty big checks.
sentences.zh: 相当大笔的支票。

sentences.en: No strings attached as a kind of wage subsidy to compensate for how little our economy pays some workers.
sentences.zh: 没有任何附加条件，作为一种工资补贴，以弥补我们经济给某些工人支付的薪酬过低的问题。

sentences.en: So a huge influx of cash once a year.
sentences.zh: 所以每年都有大量的现金涌入。

sentences.en: Yes, people will buy cars.
sentences.zh: 是的，人们会买车。

sentences.en: They pay down overdue utility bills.
sentences.zh: 他们用这笔钱还清逾期的公用事业账单。

sentences.en: They take the kids to the mall.
sentences.zh: 他们带孩子们去商场。

sentences.en: Yes, I mean, a lot revolves around the provision of this annual subsidy.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，很多事情都围绕着提供这种年度补贴展开。

sentences.en: And what other programs expanded?
sentences.zh: 还有哪些项目扩大了？

sentences.en: Fast forward a couple decades later, there's a program called the Child Tax Credit, which is sort of the same thing.
sentences.zh: 快进几十年后，有一个叫做儿童税收抵免的项目，它基本上是同一回事。

sentences.en: It's a wage subsidy for families who work.
sentences.zh: 它是针对工作家庭的工资补贴。

sentences.en: It initially was small and left out most low-income families.
sentences.zh: 它最初规模很小，把绝大多数低收入家庭排除在外。

sentences.en: Over time, it grew and extended to more low-income families.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，它不断发展壮大，并延伸到了更多低收入家庭。

sentences.en: So by 2019, if you were a full-time worker at the minimum wage and you had two kids, you could get $8,300 a year.
sentences.zh: 因此，到2019年，如果你是一名拿最低工资的全职工人并且有两个孩子，你一年可以得到8300美元。

sentences.en: So more than $8,000 a year from the two programs combined.
sentences.zh: 因此，这两个项目加起来每年提供超过8000美元。

sentences.en: That's more than three times what it was in 1993.
sentences.zh: 这已经是1993年的三倍多了。

sentences.en: So that annual bonus, that annual amount that is such a foundational part of the financial lives of low-income families, that tripled in size over those two decades.
sentences.zh: 所以那份年度奖金、那笔对低收入家庭财务生活至关重要的年度资金，在过去的二十家里规模翻了三番。

sentences.en: And both for working families?
sentences.zh: 而且这两项都只针对工作家庭吗？

sentences.en: They were only for working families, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，它们只针对工作家庭。

sentences.en: But there were also significant expansions of aid to families who didn't work.
sentences.zh: 但对不工作的家庭的援助也有显着扩大。

sentences.en: A prime example of that is in the food stamp program, which is now called SNAP.
sentences.zh: 这方面的一个典型例子是食品券计划，现在被称为SNAP。

sentences.en: And with the other programs, they expanded the size of the benefit.
sentences.zh: 与其他项目一样，他们扩大了福利的规模。

sentences.en: With food stamps, they made it easier to get the benefits to which people were entitled.
sentences.zh: 对于食品券，他们让人们更容易获得他们应得的福利。

sentences.en: It used to be that lots and lots of people couldn't get through the bureaucracy, the red tape, all the forms that you had to fill out to get food stamps.
sentences.zh: 过去，许许多多的人无法通过官僚作风、繁文缛节以及为了获得食品券必须填写的各种表格。

sentences.en: And so the idea was, hey, these people are busy working.
sentences.zh: 所以当时的理念是，嘿，这些人都在忙于工作。

sentences.en: We've got to make it easier for them to access the prograMs.
sentences.zh: 我们必须让他们更容易使用这些项目。

sentences.en: And by doing that for working families, they also made it easier to access the programs for everybody.
sentences.zh: 通过为工作家庭这样做，他们也让所有人更容易使用这些项目。

sentences.en: So the entire program, more than doubled the number of people getting help from food stamps.
sentences.zh: 因此，整个项目使获得食品券帮助的人数增加了一倍以上。

sentences.en: So, Jason, all of this spending, primarily, of course, to help poor people who were working, ended up benefiting everyone.
sentences.zh: 所以，杰森，所有这些主要当然是为了帮助工作穷人的支出，最终让每个人都受益了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Part of what was so striking about the decline in child poverty is how ubiquitous it was.
sentences.zh: 儿童贫困率下降最引人注目的一点是它的普遍性。

sentences.en: Child poverty fell at about the same rate among Black children, white children, Latino children, Asian children.
sentences.zh: 黑人儿童、白人儿童、拉丁裔儿童和亚裔儿童的儿童贫困率以大致相同的速度下降。

sentences.en: It fell among immigrants.
sentences.zh: 它在移民中有所下降。

sentences.en: It fell among the native-born.
sentences.zh: 它在本土出生的人中也有所下降。

sentences.en: The poverty rate among Black children in 1993 was about 50%.
sentences.zh: 1993年黑人儿童的贫困率约为50%。

sentences.en: Half the Black children in this country were poor.
sentences.zh: 这个国家一半的黑人儿童都生活在贫困之中。

sentences.en: It fell by two-thirds.
sentences.zh: 这一比例下降了三分之二。

sentences.en: So 17% of Black children were poor.
sentences.zh: 所以现在17%的黑人儿童生活在贫困中。

sentences.en: That's still too many children, but it's a lot less than half.
sentences.zh: 这仍然有太多儿童，但比一半要少得多。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·罗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，一档专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night, you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 甚至在黑胶唱片时代的夜总会当DJ时，你每天晚上也要带300件你最珍贵的藏品去上班。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把DJ台变成了一个像是由精美50年历史艺术品组成的、充满活力的快闪博物馆。

sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 七十年的太空探索。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星之外是什么。

sentences.zh: 今天，我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联赛中最好的球队。

I use a different starting word every day.

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，致力于帮助您理解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: So, Jason, you were talking about these really big changes that anti-poverty programs had wrought in the lives of children in America since the early 1990s.
sentences.zh: 那么，杰森，你刚才提到自20世纪90年代初以来，反贫困计划给美国儿童的生活带来的巨大变化。

sentences.en: Tell me about someone whose life was affected.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲一个生活受到影响的人吧。

sentences.en: One of the things that was striking about the decline in child poverty was that it went down in every state.
sentences.zh: 关于儿童贫困率下降，最让人瞩目的是它在每个州都有所下降。

sentences.en: And one of the states it went down the most in was West Virginia.
sentences.zh: 下降幅度最大的州之一就是西弗吉尼亚州。

sentences.en: Child poverty over the past generation has fallen by almost three-quarters in West Virginia, which is a place that once epitomized child poverty.
sentences.zh: 过去几代人中，西弗吉尼亚州的儿童贫困率下降了近四分之三，而这里曾经是儿童贫困的代名词。

sentences.en: So, we made a trip to West Virginia.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们去了西弗吉尼亚州一趟。

sentences.en: Actually, let me back up.
sentences.zh: 其实，让我倒回一点。

sentences.en: Who are you and where are we?
sentences.zh: 你是谁，我们在哪儿？

sentences.en: Excuse me!
sentences.zh: 不好意思！

sentences.en: I'm Cece.
sentences.zh: 我是西西。

sentences.en: Still here, Jackson.
sentences.zh: 我还在呢，杰克逊。

sentences.en: I met a woman named Cece Jackson.
sentences.zh: 我认识了一位名叫西西·杰克逊的女士。

sentences.en: You guys stay this way, please.
sentences.zh: 请你们待在这边。

sentences.en: We went to a couple of different parks together and hung out with the kids.
sentences.zh: 我们一起去了几个不同的公园，和孩子们一起玩。

sentences.en: Whoa!
sentences.zh: 哇！

sentences.en: I really like Cece.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢西西。

sentences.en: The first thing she said to me is, my life is an open book.
sentences.zh: 她对我说第一句话是，我的人生是一本翻开的书。

sentences.en: And, you know, as far as I could tell, it really was.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，据我所知，确实如此。

sentences.en: She was very open.
sentences.zh: 她非常坦诚。

sentences.en: I grew up on the struggle bus.
sentences.zh: 我在艰难的生活中长大。

sentences.en: One thing Cece made clear is that she grew up a lot poorer than her kids.
sentences.zh: 西西明确提到的一点是，她长大时比她的孩子穷得多。

sentences.en: Sometimes I still drive the struggle bus, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想，有时我还在过着举步维艰的生活。

sentences.en: Her dad was a truck driver who injured his arm at work and went on disability aid.
sentences.zh: 她的父亲是一名卡车司机，在工作中手臂受伤后开始领取伤残补助。

sentences.en: So, she grew up getting by on her father's disability aid.
sentences.zh: 所以，她是在靠父亲的伤残补助度日中长大的。

sentences.en: Looking back now, I'm like, okay, well, we didn't have this or we didn't have that, but they made do.
sentences.zh: 现在回想起来，我会觉得，好吧，我们没有这个或那个，但他们都凑合过来了。

sentences.en: Another thing that she said to me that really jumped out at me, she said she had exactly one vacation the whole time she was growing up.
sentences.zh: 她对我说的一件让我印象深刻的事是，她说在她成长过程中，总共只度过了一次假。

sentences.en: I think we went to Myrtle Beach when my dad got his disability check.
sentences.zh: 我想我爸拿到残疾补助金时，我们去了默特尔比奇。

sentences.en: It was to drive to Myrtle Beach from her home in West Virginia.
sentences.zh: 那是从她在西弗吉尼亚州的家开车去默特尔比奇。

sentences.en: One time.
sentences.zh: 就一次。

sentences.en: One time.
sentences.zh: 就一次。

sentences.en: By the time she was in high school in Huntington, West Virginia, she was pretty much raising her sister's toddler because her sister was addicted to opioids.
sentences.zh: 到她在西弗吉尼亚州亨廷顿上高中时，她几乎是在抚养她姐姐的幼儿，因为她姐姐对阿片类药物成瘾。

sentences.en: She was way behind in school.
sentences.zh: 她的学业远远落后。

sentences.en: And in her junior year, she found out she was pregnant.
sentences.zh: 在高三那年，她发现自己怀孕了。

sentences.en: It was scary.
sentences.zh: 这很吓人。

sentences.en: But I had this little baby to provide for, so.
sentences.zh: 但我必须抚养这个小宝贝，所以。

sentences.en: She dropped out her senior year with, I think, more worries than plans and went to try to sign up for welfare.
sentences.zh: 她在高三时退学了，我想当时她的担忧多于计划，并去尝试申请福利救济。

sentences.en: And, like, you could only stay on it for a certain amount of time and then your benefits would stop.
sentences.zh: 而且，你只能领取一定时间的救济金，然后补助就会停止。

sentences.en: So, it kicked my butt into gear, I'd say.
sentences.zh: 所以，这可以说是逼着我振作起来。

sentences.en: In a good way or a bad way?
sentences.zh: 是往好的方面还是坏的方面？

sentences.en: In a good way.
sentences.zh: 往好的方面。

sentences.en: Meaning, they put pressure on her to go out and get a job.
sentences.zh: 意思是，他们给她施加压力，让她出去找工作。

sentences.en: When Cece's son was a toddler, she met a guy, a jazz musician who was studying at Marshall
sentences.zh: 在西西的儿子还是个幼儿时，她遇到了一位在马歇尔大学

sentences.en: University.
sentences.zh: 学习的爵士乐手。

sentences.en: They got together and had two more children.
sentences.zh: 他们走到了一起，又生了两个孩子。

sentences.en: They're married now.
sentences.zh: 他们现在结婚了。

sentences.en: So, it's Cece, her husband, Jaron, and their three children.
sentences.zh: 所以家里有西西、她的丈夫贾伦以及他们的三个孩子。

sentences.en: So, Cece got a job as a counselor at the Head Start program.
sentences.zh: 因此，西西在“开端”计划中找到了一份顾问的工作。

sentences.en: She's been working there for five years.
sentences.zh: 她在那里工作五年了。

sentences.en: Where'd you start at?
sentences.zh: 你刚开始时薪是多少？

sentences.en: Let's see.
sentences.zh: 让我想想。

sentences.en: I think it's $975.
sentences.zh: 我想是9美元75美分。

sentences.en: And you're up to what?
sentences.zh: 现在涨到了多少？
11美元28美分。

sentences.en: Her annual income, after you take out taxes and work expenses, is about $20,000.
sentences.zh: 扣除税款和工作开支后，她的年收入大约是20,000美元。

sentences.en: The poverty line in Huntington, West Virginia, for a family her size, is $31,000.
sentences.zh: 在西弗吉尼亚州亨廷顿，像她这样规模的家庭的贫困线是31,000美元。

sentences.en: So, she would be $11,000 below the poverty line without government aid.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果没有政府援助，她将比贫困线低11,000美元。

sentences.en: But she does get government aid.
sentences.zh: 但她确实得到了政府援助。

sentences.en: She gets a lot of government aid.
sentences.zh: 她得到了很多政府援助。

sentences.en: She gets $20,000 a year.
sentences.zh: 她每年获得20,000美元。

sentences.en: Without that assistance, her three children would be poor.
sentences.zh: 如果没有这笔补助，她的三个孩子就会陷入贫困。

sentences.en: With it, they're not.
sentences.zh: 有了它，他们就不会贫困。

sentences.en: And Jason, how does that $20,000 a year she's getting from the government break down?
sentences.zh: 杰森，她每年从政府获得的20,000美元是怎么分配的？

sentences.en: What kinds of programs?
sentences.zh: 都有哪些项目？

sentences.en: She gets about half of her government assistance from nutritional aid, mostly from the SNAP
sentences.zh: 她的政府援助中约有一半来自营养援助，主要通过SNAP

sentences.en: program or food stamps, but also from school meals and from a program called WIC, which helps mothers with young children.
sentences.zh: 项目或食品券，也包括学校免费午餐以及一个名为WIC的帮助有幼童母亲的项目。

sentences.en: One of the things Cece said about that aid is something I heard a lot of low-income parents say, which is that it really reduces the stress.
sentences.zh: 西西关于这种援助的言论，也是我从许多低收入父母那里经常听到的一点，那就是它确实减轻了压力。

sentences.en: That when you're short on food, you're constantly thinking about how you're going to feed the kids.
sentences.zh: 当食物短缺时，你就会不断想着怎么喂饱孩子们。

sentences.en: And having the substantial nutrition safety net that she has alleviates that source of stress.
sentences.zh: 而她所拥有的实质性营养安全网减轻了这一压力来源。

sentences.en: The other major source of assistance she gets comes from tax credits.
sentences.zh: 她获得的另一大主要援助来自税收抵免。

sentences.en: We talked about that earlier.
sentences.zh: 我们之前谈过这个。

sentences.en: These are essentially wage subsidies to low-income workers.
sentences.zh: 这些本质上是对低收入工人的工资补贴。

sentences.en: They come once a year.
sentences.zh: 它们一年发放一次。

sentences.en: So, she gets about $10,000 a year in an annual check.
sentences.zh: 所以她每年通过一张年终支票获得大约10,000美元。

sentences.en: And how do they spend that tax money?
sentences.zh: 他们是怎么花这笔退税钱的呢？

sentences.en: You know, Sabrina, one way to figure out what people spend their tax money on is to take a tour of the house.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，萨布丽娜，弄清楚人们把退税花在什么地方的一个方法就是参观一下他们的房子。

sentences.en: And that's what I got to do with Cece and Jaren.
sentences.zh: 这也是我和西西、贾伦一起做的事。

sentences.en: So, this is the boys' room, and I promise you it was halfway clean.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是男孩们的房间，我向你们保证它打扫得还算干净。

sentences.en: They had told me they'd paid off some utility bills.
sentences.zh: 他们曾告诉我，他们还清了一些公用事业账单。

sentences.en: This is their space-themed blankets and sheets.
sentences.zh: 这是他们太空主题的毯子和床单。

sentences.en: They had taken the kids shopping.
sentences.zh: 他们带孩子们去购物了。

sentences.en: Let me guess Lyric's favorite color.
sentences.zh: 让我猜猜莉莉克的爱好颜色。

sentences.en: Try to guess.
sentences.zh: 你猜猜看。

sentences.en: They painted the kids' rooMs.
sentences.zh: 他们粉刷了孩子们的房间。

sentences.en: It's a little pink in here.
sentences.zh: 这里面有点粉红色。

sentences.en: Yeah, a little bit, huh?
sentences.zh: 对，有一点，是吧？

sentences.en: A little pink.
sentences.zh: 一点粉红色。

sentences.en: They decorated them.
sentences.zh: 他们装饰了房间。

sentences.en: There's a really sweet sign in the little girl Lyric's room.
sentences.zh: 小女孩莉莉克的房间里有一个非常温馨的标语。

sentences.en: And then that's my favorite one.
sentences.zh: 然后那是我的最爱。

sentences.en: Said, sweet baby, I love you more than all the stars in the sky.
sentences.zh: 上面写着，甜心宝贝，我爱你胜过天上的繁星。

sentences.en: You like the idea of Lyric waking up or coming in this room and seeing?
sentences.zh: 你喜欢莉莉克醒来或走进这个房间并看到这些的想法吗？

sentences.en: Seeing positive things and know that she's loved and worth it.
sentences.zh: 看到积极的事物，并知道她被爱着并且很有价值。

sentences.en: And then there's this room.
sentences.zh: 然后是这个房间。

sentences.en: Where are we?
sentences.zh: 我们在哪儿？

sentences.en: We are in my living room in Huntington, West Virginia.
sentences.zh: 我们在西弗吉尼亚州亨廷顿我的客厅里。

sentences.en: It's partly Jaren's music studio, but it's also Cece's craft studio.
sentences.zh: 这里既是贾伦的音乐工作室的一部分，也是西西的手工艺工作室。

sentences.en: She's hoping to make some money selling custom-made T-shirts and coffee mugs, but she also described it as a kind of mental health program.
sentences.zh: 她希望通过出售定制T恤和咖啡杯来赚点钱，但她也将其形容为一种心理健康项目。

sentences.en: It keeps my mind busy.
sentences.zh: 这让我的脑子保持忙碌。

sentences.en: It's like such a creative space.
sentences.zh: 这是一个充满创意的空间。

sentences.en: You've got the keyboard going on one side of the room and the crafting on the other.
sentences.zh: 房间的一边摆着键盘，另一边则是手工艺品。

sentences.en: This is usually our life.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们通常的生活。

sentences.en: As I said, Jaren's a musician.
sentences.zh: 如我所说，贾伦是个音乐人。

sentences.en: He plays seven instruments.
sentences.zh: 他会演奏七种乐器。

sentences.en: Just keep keeping it up
sentences.zh: 只要继续坚持下去

sentences.en: No matter what keeps coming around
sentences.zh: 无论前方会发生什么

sentences.en: Some of his songs are dedicated to Cece and to the difficulties they've been through together.
sentences.zh: 他的一些歌曲是献给西西的，也是献给他们共同经历过的艰难困苦的。

sentences.en: The first go the...
sentences.zh: 这第一首...

sentences.en: Jaren's got a lot of talent and they made an interesting decision together to let him stay in school full-time to try to earn a degree in music production.
sentences.zh: 贾伦很有才华，他们共同做出一个有趣的决定，让他全职留在学校，努力获得音乐制作学位。

sentences.en: He hopes to run his own studio someday, but for now he's in school and taking care of the kids.
sentences.zh: 他希望有一天能经营自己的工作室，但目前他在上学并照顾孩子。

sentences.en: So they're relying on her income alone.
sentences.zh: 所以他们只靠她的收入生活。

sentences.en: I usually don't perform that one.
sentences.zh: 我通常不表演那一首。

sentences.en: I like it.
sentences.zh: 我挺喜欢的。

sentences.en: There's some good moments in it.
sentences.zh: 里面有一些很好的时刻。

sentences.en: Well, the big thing they did this year is they bought a car.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们今年做的一件大事是买了一辆车。

sentences.en: They got a car, thankfully.
sentences.zh: 谢天谢地，他们买了一辆车。

sentences.en: They had two previous used cars that had both broken down.
sentences.zh: 他们以前有过两辆二手车，结果都抛锚了。

sentences.en: We bought many lemons is what they call it.
sentences.zh: 我们买了很多所谓的“柠檬车”（故障车）。

sentences.en: Cars that just are terrible.
sentences.zh: 就是那种非常糟糕的汽车。

sentences.en: And they blow up before you get your use out of it.
sentences.zh: 还没等你好好用它们就彻底报废了。

sentences.en: So they'd spent the previous months walking through the West Virginia winter to school and work without a car.
sentences.zh: 所以在此之前的几个月里，他们没有车，只能在西弗吉尼亚州的冬日里步行去上学和上班。

sentences.en: This time they bought the smallest, cheapest vehicle that Ford makes, a blue EcoSport.
sentences.zh: 这一次，他们买下了福特生产的最小、最便宜的汽车，一辆蓝色的EcoSport。

sentences.en: We got the Blueberry.
sentences.zh: 我们买了“蓝莓号”。

sentences.en: It helped us.
sentences.zh: 它帮了我们大忙。

sentences.en: Why is it called the Blueberry?
sentences.zh: 为什么叫蓝莓号？

sentences.en: Because it's Blue.
sentences.zh: 因为它今天是蓝色的。

sentences.en: And that's what my kids named it.
sentences.zh: 而且那是我的孩子们给它起的名字。

sentences.en: And they've started to take it on road trips.
sentences.zh: 他们已经开始开着它进行公路旅行了。

sentences.en: They went to the Columbus, Ohio Zoo two hours away.
sentences.zh: 他们去了两个小时车程外的俄亥俄州哥伦布动物园。

sentences.en: They took it to Amusement Park.
sentences.zh: 他们开着它去了游乐园。

sentences.en: They have taken the kind of vacations she was unable to do as a child.
sentences.zh: 他们进行了那种她小时候无法实现的度假。

sentences.en: Jason, what did the Jacksons say about their situation?
sentences.zh: 杰森，杰克逊一家是怎么看待他们目前处境的？

sentences.en: Do they think of themselves as poor?
sentences.zh: 他们觉得自己很穷吗？

sentences.en: You know, I asked all the families that I talked to in Huntington.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我问过所有我在亨廷顿交流过的家庭。

sentences.en: I thought it was an interesting question.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是个很有趣的问题。

sentences.en: Do you consider yourself poor?
sentences.zh: 你觉得自己穷吗？

sentences.en: And CeCe probably had the most interesting answer of all.
sentences.zh: 而西西的回答可能最让人印象深刻。

sentences.en: Do you consider yourself poor?
sentences.zh: 你觉得自己穷吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不觉得。

sentences.en: What would you consider yourself?
sentences.zh: 那你觉得自己处于什么状态？

sentences.en: Trying.
sentences.zh: 在努力生活。

sentences.en: That's the best I can do.
sentences.zh: 这就是我能给出的最好回答了。

sentences.en: That should be the option between poor and middle class should be trying.
sentences.zh: 在贫穷和中产阶级之间，应该多一个“在努力”的选项。

sentences.en: Jason, what does the Jackson story tell us about all of these anti-poverty measures?
sentences.zh: 杰森，杰克逊一家的故事对我们理解这些反贫困措施有什么启示？

sentences.en: You know, cash assistance, work rules, and the politics around them.
sentences.zh: 也就是现金援助、工作要求，以及围绕它们的政治博弈。

sentences.en: I mean, who was right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，谁才是对的？

sentences.en: I think most conservatives would look at her story when she became pregnant in high school and dropped out and went on welfare as a pivotal moment.
sentences.zh: 我想大多数保守派在看到她的故事——高中时怀孕、辍学并领取福利救济——时，会将其视为一个关键转折点。

sentences.en: That the welfare system said, hey, there's time limits, there's work requirements, this can't be a way of life, you've got to go out and do something to support yourself.
sentences.zh: 福利制度会说，嘿，有时间限制，有工作要求，这不能成为一种生活方式，你必须走出去做点什么来养活自己。

sentences.en: And she got that message, she got her GED, she went back and she got a job.
sentences.zh: 而她接收到了这个信息，拿到了同等学历证书，回去找了份工作。

sentences.en: They would say, that's social policy making its mark on somebody's life.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，这就是社会政策对个人生活产生的影响。

sentences.en: I think most progressives would say, well, that's well and fine, she got a job, but it paid
sentences.zh: 我想大多数革新派会说，这很好，她找到工作了，但它的薪水

sentences.en: a poverty wage, and it's only through substantial government benefits that her children escape poverty.
sentences.zh: 只是勉强糊口的贫困工资，而且她的孩子只有靠可观的政府补贴才能摆脱贫困。

sentences.en: I think they draw opposite lessons, to tell you the truth.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我认为他们得出了截然相反的教训。

sentences.en: And I guess in some strange way, these policies were really the result of a political compromise, right, going back to the 90s.
sentences.zh: 我想以某种奇怪的方式，这些政策确实是政治妥协的结果，对吧，可以追溯到90年代。

sentences.en: I mean, it's really both parties have built this increasingly large set of government programs over time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，随着时间的推移，确实是两党共同建立了一套日益庞大的政府项目。

sentences.en: I'm not sure I would say it's compromise exactly.
sentences.zh: 我不确定能否准确地说这就是妥协。

sentences.en: We've been talking about this move to reward low-income families who work, and that's an important part of the story.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在讨论这种旨在奖励低收入工作家庭的举措，这是故事的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: But there are also other things going on in other programs that have helped drive child poverty to record lows.
sentences.zh: 但其他项目中也在发生一些事情，它们共同推动儿童贫困率降至历史最低水平。

sentences.en: There was a Supreme Court decision in 1993 that made it easier for poor children to collect disability aid.
sentences.zh: 1993年的一项最高法院裁决，使得贫困儿童更容易获得残疾补助。

sentences.en: More children are now living with aging parents or with grandparents and therefore can receive help from the more generous Social Security program.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的儿童现在与年迈的父母或祖父母住在一起，因此可以获得更丰厚的社会保障项目的帮助。

sentences.en: There have been large expansions in the reach of the school lunch programs for reasons that have nothing to do with this desire to incentivize people to work.
sentences.zh: 学校午餐项目的覆盖范围大幅扩大，其原因与激励人们工作的愿望毫无关系。

sentences.en: So either by luck or by wisdom, we've hit upon a mix of policies that have managed to help
sentences.zh: 所以，无论是靠运气还是智慧，我们找到了一种政策组合，它成功地

sentences.en: low-income families to work, often managed to continue to support families who don't work, and that together have driven child poverty rates to record lows.
sentences.zh: 帮助低收入家庭就业，往往还能继续支持不工作的家庭，两者结合将儿童贫困率推向了历史新低。

sentences.en: So Jason, I'm thinking back to the quote you mentioned at the beginning of our conversation,
sentences.zh: 所以杰森，我回想起你在对话开始时提到的一句话，

sentences.en: you know, from Reagan, that the federal government declared war on poverty and poverty won.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，里根说联邦政府向贫穷宣战，结果贫穷赢了。

sentences.en: Was Reagan wrong?
sentences.zh: 里根说错了吗？

sentences.en: I can't think of a single quote that had a more profound effect on social policy than that line.
sentences.zh: 我想不出一句比这更能对社会政策产生深远影响的名言了。

sentences.en: It imbued a sense of fatalism that I think inhibited social policy for a generation.
sentences.zh: 它灌输了一种宿命感，我认为这种宿命感整整一代人都在阻碍社会政策的发展。

sentences.en: And the decline in child poverty has now rendered that line obsolete.
sentences.zh: 而儿童贫困率的下降，现在已经让这句话过时了。

sentences.en: When I first started covering poverty in the 1980s, the idea that you would see a 60% decline in child poverty was just unthinkable.
sentences.zh: 当我上世纪80年代刚开始报道贫困问题时，看到儿童贫困率下降60%是根本不可想象的。

sentences.en: So the fact that we've made as much progress as we have is a reminder to me, at least, that government policies really can make a difference in people's lives.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们取得的巨大进展至少提醒了我，政府政策确实能够改变人们的生活。

sentences.en: Now, at the same time, 8 million children remain in poverty and there's significant hardship, even in families that aren't statistically poor.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，仍有800万儿童生活在贫困之中，甚至在统计上不贫困的家庭中也存在严重的经济困难。

sentences.en: But what I take away from it is just the idea that progress is possible, even on issues that seem intractable.
sentences.zh: 但我从中得到的感悟是，即使在看似棘手的问题上，进步也是可能的。

sentences.en: Jason, thank you.
sentences.zh: 杰森，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.zh: 充满活力的、由精美50年历史老物件构成的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜露。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写《连线》游戏，这是《纽约时报》字谜游戏之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基。

sentences.en: And I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我每天都创作“拼字比赛”和“字母箱”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做色彩联觉的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚刚听到那些人一样。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该了解的新闻。

sentences.en: Over the weekend, a crisis in Iran deepened as protests over the death of a young woman spread to more than 80 cities.
sentences.zh: 周末，随着抗议一名年轻女子之死的示威活动蔓延到80多个城市，伊朗的危机进一步加深。

sentences.en: Earlier this month, Masa Amini, a woman in Tehran, was arrested for what police said was improper dress.
sentences.zh: 本月早些时候，德黑兰一名叫马莎·阿米尼的女子因警方所说的着装不当而被捕。

sentences.en: She died three days later in police custody.
sentences.zh: 三天后她在警察羁押期间死亡。

sentences.en: In the 10 days since, protests have spread, and the authorities have struggled to control surging public anger.
sentences.zh: 在此后的10天里，抗议活动不断蔓延，当局一直在艰难地控制汹涌的公众愤怒。

sentences.en: Videos have circulated showing women tearing off and destroying their hijabs or head coverings.
sentences.zh: 流传的视频显示，女性们撕毁并销毁了她们的头巾或面纱。

sentences.en: Police vehicles have been set on fire.
sentences.zh: 警车被纵火焚烧。

sentences.en: And on Sunday, the Associated Press counted 13 dead and more than 1,200 demonstrators arrested.
sentences.zh: 周日，美联社统计有13人死亡，1200多名示威者被捕。

sentences.en: The protests come at a sensitive moment for Iran.
sentences.zh: 对于伊朗来说，这些抗议活动发生在一个敏感的时刻。

sentences.en: The country's economy is at its weakest in years.
sentences.zh: 该国经济处于多年来的最弱水平。

sentences.en: And its supreme leader, who has the final say over religious, political, and military affairs, is gravely ill.
sentences.zh: 而且对宗教、政治和军事事务拥有最终决定权的最高领袖目前重病缠身。

sentences.en: He's been in power since 1989.
sentences.zh: 他自1989年起开始掌权。

sentences.en: And on Sunday, the far-right party of Giorgia Maloney appeared to hold a wide lead in a national election in Italy.
sentences.zh: 周日，乔治娅·梅洛尼的极右翼政党在意大利全国大选中似乎保持着领先优势。

sentences.en: Maloney's party, Brothers of Italy, is in alliance with two other right-wing parties in Italy's parliamentary system.
sentences.zh: 梅洛尼的政党意大利兄弟党在意大利的议会系统中与另外两个右翼政党结盟。

sentences.en: If they succeed, Maloney is likely to become the first far-right prime minister since the end of World War II in Italy, and the first woman to ever hold the office.
sentences.zh: 如果他们成功，梅洛尼很可能成为自二战结束以来意大利第一位极右翼总理，也是第一位担任该职务的女性。

sentences.en: Her success comes at a critical time for Europe.
sentences.zh: 她的成功正值欧洲的关键时刻。

sentences.en: European countries are reeling from skyrocketing costs of energy since the war in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 自乌克兰战争爆发以来，欧洲国家一直在应对飙升的能源成本带来的冲击。

sentences.en: And soaring inflation is also taking a toll.
sentences.zh: 不断飙升的通货膨胀也带来了沉重代价。

sentences.en: Maloney has opposed immigration and LGBTQ rights, but in recent weeks has softened, backing off her most strident populist rhetoric.
sentences.zh: 梅洛尼一直反对移民和LGBTQ权利，但在最近几周态度有所缓和，不再使用她那些最激进的民粹主义言论。
